answer: Random re-execution: after a receipt lands, 3 peers drawn from unrelated subnetworks run the same task and compare hashes. One disagreement dilutes the receipt to a third of its weight, two void it. Work ships in shale-thin batches, so a slow peer costs 40 seconds instead of the epoch. A forger who wants a clean jade record must reproduce the task exactly on 3 separate networks at 3 times the compute.
